briefing.opening: Good morning/afternoon, everyone. I will now begin the climate briefing for September 4, 2026.

sections.title: 🔴 Deepening Climate Crisis and Global Disaster Warnings
sections.content: The United Nations (UN) has declared the collapse of the 1.5-degree global warming defense line, warning of the severity of the climate crisis [16, 134, 140]. Globally, 40-degree heatwaves are becoming the new normal [11], and the El Niño phenomenon is intensifying due to human-induced climate change, necessitating preparations for a 'super' El Niño [136, 137, 145, 146, 154]. Particularly in Nepal, large-scale flood disasters have occurred consecutively, displacing numerous people and urgently requiring housing reconstruction [19, 21, 129, 131, 133, 141, 142, 153, 159]. In Jeju, typhoon-level strong winds have caused widespread damage [130], highlighting the severity of climate disasters across the globe [4, 6, 24, 148, 161]. Such climate change is triggering supply chain shocks [4, 149], exacerbating difficulties for fishing communities due to warming oceans [10], and demonstrating the urgent need for adaptation measures such as changes in park and forest management practices [17, 25]. Furthermore, the impacts of climate change are manifesting across all sectors, with Australian ski resorts closing up to a month early due to record heatwaves and limited snowfall [158].

sections.title: 🌱 Domestic and International Climate Change Response Efforts and Expanded Cooperation
sections.content: Despite the deepening climate crisis, various domestic and international response efforts are continuing. In Busan, the Partnerships in Environmental Management for the Seas of East Asia (PEMSEA) Forum was held to discuss environmental issues including climate change [1, 3, 7]. South Korea and Laos have initiated a climate change response project through forestry [2], and South Korea and China have resumed dialogues on global food security and climate change crisis response [8]. Domestically, the Daejeon City Council has laid the groundwork for establishing a rapid response system for climate change and invasive pests [9, 18, 22]. Gyeongnam Province is introducing pre-analysis of climate risks in the design of public buildings to create structures resilient to heatwaves and flooding [23, 27]. Furthermore, Hyundai Motor Group has signed an MOU with Oman for eco-friendly mobility, contributing to accelerating the carbon-neutral transition [37, 38, 49, 54, 57, 58, 61, 63, 65, 69, 81, 84]. Industrial participation is also active, with Samsung C&T and POSCO targeting global carbon neutrality through next-generation nuclear power plants and eco-friendly steelmaking [66].

sections.title: 🇰🇷 Accelerating Community-Led Carbon Neutrality Initiatives
sections.content: Efforts to achieve carbon neutrality are also expanding at the community level. Gwacheon City is building a network encompassing seven districts, businesses, and institutions, aiming for 'One Institution, One Carbon Neutrality Practice' to expand participation from residents and companies [29, 30, 31, 43, 45, 52, 64, 72]. Gyeongnam Province is promoting carbon neutrality practices by reducing discarded banners [32]. Notably, Yesan County became the first in Chungcheongnam-do to draft a greenhouse gas reduction-aware budget, taking the first step towards carbon-neutral finance [34, 47, 60, 62, 74, 83]. The Mayor of Guri City emphasized that local communities are key actors in climate crisis response and declared a strengthening of carbon neutrality policies [26, 75]. In addition, the participation of various stakeholders, such as Mapo-gu's early childhood environmental education [46, 68] and Seocheon County's Rural Leaders' Association's agricultural waste collection activities [56, 79, 80], is contributing to the realization of carbon neutrality.

sections.title: 🌱 Accelerating Renewable Energy Transition and Current Challenges
sections.content: The transition to renewable energy is accelerating further. SK E&S and Enlighten are expanding cooperation across the entire lifecycle of renewable energy projects, including solar power [85, 88, 89, 91, 97, 103, 108, 123]. Local governments such as Gunsan City and Changwon City are providing subsidies for household solar panel installations, aiming to expand their adoption [92, 106, 120, 127]. Notably, with analyses suggesting that combining renewable energy with batteries is cost-effective and more competitive than nuclear power [94, 95, 98], efforts to enhance grid stability are also underway, including expanding mandatory renewable energy monitoring and increasing the number of generators subject to remote output control installation [87, 101, 104, 113, 126]. Furthermore, new renewable energy expansion and generation have reached record levels in the United States and Northern Ireland [111, 156, 160]. Five power generation companies are planning to integrate to strengthen their role as key implementers of renewable energy [99, 112, 114, 128]. However, new challenges arising from the expansion of renewable energy are also being raised, such as safety accident issues with aging renewable energy facilities [93] and the projected 10,000 tons of discarded solar panels by 2032 [105], as highlighted in the 2026 parliamentary audit [35, 117].

sections.title: ⚠️ Fossil Fuel Development Discussions and Conflict with Climate Goals
sections.content: Despite the deepening climate crisis and carbon neutrality efforts, discussions on fossil fuel development continue, raising concerns. News has emerged that the controversial Jackdaw gas field in the UK North Sea is expected to receive ministerial approval this month, with the Rosebank oil field approval also being considered by the end of this year [157]. Such fossil fuel development plans could make achieving the 1.5-degree global warming limit target even more challenging [134] and may conflict with the global goal of transitioning to carbon neutrality, thus requiring continuous monitoring and critical discussion [159]. Discussions have also arisen regarding whether the 'three major mega-projects' related to AI and semiconductors are compatible with carbon neutrality goals [35], necessitating a cautious approach for sustainable development.

briefing.closing: In today's briefing, we observed the deepening global climate crisis, alongside various domestic and international cooperation efforts and renewable energy transition initiatives aimed at overcoming it. Recognizing the urgency of responding to the climate crisis, substantive actions and policy support for a sustainable future must be further strengthened. This concludes today's climate briefing.
